title: Why Products Grow Up Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 17
description:
Laddoo Lab's six-pack was a hit, and every week more families bought it. Then sales stopped growing. Is Zoya's laddoo dying? No. It is just growing up. In this animated lesson we use one millet laddoo six-pack from a Bengaluru home kitchen to understand the product life cycle.

You will see Kotler and Armstrong's definition, how Theodore Levitt made the idea famous in the Harvard Business Review in 1965, and a live run of the six-pack's sales and profit curve through introduction, growth, maturity and decline. We look at the plan each stage needs, three ways to refresh a mature product (new users, a new product, a new mix), and the life cycle at work today: a scooter maker's free test rides, a delivery app opening new cities, a toothpaste maker adding flavours, and music CDs fading as streaming arrived. Then the human side: the curve is a useful map, but stages are often seen only looking back, and Dhalla and Yuspeh warned in the Harvard Business Review in 1976 that it can push firms to drop healthy products too soon.

This is Episode 17 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
